THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 05.06.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:39518 WPC.No.14318/25 3  JUDGMENT
The petitioner is a dealer of the TATA Motors and the first opposite party in CC.No.186/2023 on the file of the Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Kannur.
The said complaint was filed by the 2nd respondent alleging deficiency of service against the petitioner and the second opposite party therein, the manufacturer of the said vehicle.

As per Ext.P1 order, the complaint was allowed directing the opposite parties therein to replace the vehicle supplied by the 1 st petitioner, and to pay Rs.2,50,000/- towards the compensation and monthly loss, along with Rs.10,000/- as cost.
It was further directed that in case the opposite parties fail to replace the vehicle, an amount of Rs.19,79,082/- with 7% interest per annum till the date of realization shall be paid.
2. Challenging Ext.P1, the petitioner submitted Ext.P2 appeal before the Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, which is numbered as FA.No.92 of 2025.

entities.text: Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said appeal was filed along with the application to condone the delay 2025:KER:39518 of 407 days and a copy of the said petition is produced as Ext.P4.
Ext .P5 is the application submitted by the petitioner for stay of Ext.P1 proceedings pending consideration of the same.

It is also pointed out that the 2nd opposite party in the complaint has already approached the said Commission by filing Appeal No.158/2024,
in which Ext.P6 order of stay is passed, as regards the proceedings against the said opposite party.

Since the execution proceedings are being pursued during the pendency of this writ petition, against the petitioner, this writ petition is filed seeking the following reliefs:
"i. Issue a writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or directing the Kerala State Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission to consider and pass orders on Exhibit P5 application for stay at the earliest or within the time period fixed by this Honourable Court.
ii. Petitioner may be permitted to dispense with the filing of translation of the vernacular documents.
iii. Issue such other writ, order or direction as the Court may deem fit to grant in the circumstances of the case"
3.

sentences.text: A counter affidavit has been filed by the respondents 2, opposing the relief sought for.
4. I have heard Sri.C.Muralikrishnan, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.P.B.Biju, learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent.

5. The limited relief sought by the petitioner is to direct the State Commission to dispose of Exts.P4 and P5 applications which are now pending consideration and to keep the coercive proceedings pursuant to Ext.P1 in abeyance until such a decision is taken.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent opposed the contention by pointing out that as per Section 58(1) (b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the petitioner has a remedy of revision before the National Commission in case the State Commission failed to exercise the jurisdiction so vested, or has acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction 2025:KER:39518 illegally or with material irregularity.
Therefore, it was pointed out that this writ petition need not be entertained.

7. However, after carefully going through the entire materials placed before this Court, I am of the view that, as the appeal submitted by the petitioner along with the petition to condone the delay in filing the appeal is pending consideration, it is only proper that the same is disposed of as expeditiously as possible.

As far the coercive proceedings initiated against the petitioner are concerned, one important aspect to be noticed is that the 2nd opposite party in the complaint has already approached the State Commission and obtained Ext.P6 order against the implementation of directions in Ext.P1 order against the said party.
The directions contained in Ext.P1 are against the petitioner as well as the 2 nd opposite party therein, and those are to be performed jointly by the petitioner and the 2 nd opposite party.
Therefore, the fact that, there is already an order of stay of execution of the order against the 2nd opposite party is a relevant factor which cannot be ignored.
Moreoever, now the petitioner also has invoked the statutory remedy even though 2025:KER:39518 belatedly.
As far as the delay in filing the appeal is concerned, it is for the State Commission to consider whether it is necessary to condone the same, after hearing all the parties concerned.
Further, taking note of all the aforesaid facts, this Court has already granted an interim order in favour of the petitioner.

8. As regards the contention raised by the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent with regard to the alternate remedy of approaching the National Commission, I find that, in view of the fact that relief sought by the petitioner is very limited; i.e., to direct the State Commission to consider the application submitted by the petitioner to condone the delay and to stay the proceedings, I do not find it necessary to relegate the petitioner to invoke the statutory remedies pointed out by the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent.
While taking the above view, I have also taken note of Ext.P6 interim order passed by the State Commission in the appeal, passed in favour of the 2 nd opposite party.

In such circumstances, this writ petition is disposed of directing the Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal 2025:KER:39518 Commission, Thiruvananthapuram, to pass orders on Exts.P4 Arya Tata vs State Of Kerala on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100734280/
3 and P5 applications as expeditiously as possible after hearing the parties concerned.
